He greeted almost everyone by name, asking about someone’s knee surgery, complimenting another’s new flowers, and promising to fix a porch light next week. The silver-gray hair suited him even more in daylight, and the older residents clearly adored him. He was the neighborhood heartthrob, no question.

But their attention quickly shifted.

“And who is this?” a sharp-eyed woman in her seventies asked, openly looking Mydei up and down. “You’ve never brought anyone here before, Phainon.”

Suddenly Mydei found himself at the center of curious stares from half a dozen elderly neighbors. A few even stood up from their benches to get a better look.

Phainon grinned and casually slid an arm around Mydei’s waist, pulling him closer.

“This is Mydei,” he said proudly. “He moved here from the city a while ago. He’s… important to me.”

The reactions were immediate.

“Ohhh,” one lady cooed. “He’s very handsome!”

“Is he treating you well?” an old man asked Mydei directly, squinting. “Because if he gives you any trouble, you come tell us. We raised this boy. We can still scold him.”

Mydei felt his ears growing warm but managed a polite smile. “He’s been very good to me, actually.”

Phainon chuckled beside him. “See? I told you they’d like you.”

A small crowd had formed now. Someone asked what Mydei did for a living. Another wanted to know how they met. One particularly bold grandma even reached up to pinch Mydei’s cheek.

“You look like a good boy. Strong hands. You’ll help carry my groceries sometimes, yes?”

Phainon finally rescued him, laughing as he gently steered Mydei toward one of the buildings.

“Alright, alright, let him breathe! We’re here to see grandma. You can interrogate him more later.”

As they climbed the stairs, Phainon leaned in and whispered against Mydei’s ear, “Sorry. I should’ve warned you they’re worse than the village market crowd.”

Mydei exhaled. “They’re intense, but nice.”

Phainon stopped in front of a pale blue door on the second floor, gave Mydei’s hand a reassuring squeeze, and knocked. A moment later, the door opened.

Phainon’s grandmother was a small but formidable-looking woman in her late seventies. She had sharp eyes just like her grandson’s, silver hair pinned neatly, and a wooden spoon in her hand. The moment she saw Phainon, her face lit up with love, then her gaze landed on Mydei and her eyebrows rose with clear interest.

“Grandma,” Phainon said warmly, stepping forward to kiss her on both cheeks. “I brought someone I want you to meet.”

He gently pulled Mydei forward.

“This is Mydei.”

The old woman studied Mydei for a long, quiet moment. Then a slow, knowing smile spread across her face.

“Well… don’t just stand there,” she said, stepping aside. “Come in, come in. I hope you’re hungry.”

Phainon gave Mydei an encouraging look, his hand warm against the small of Mydei’s back as they stepped inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Yiayia
chapters.html:
Mydei sat on the old sofa while Phainon’s grandmother, who insisted he call her Yiayia, brought over a tray of cold water and biscuits.

She wasted no time. “So, Mydei,” she began with a sharp but kind smile, “where are you from originally? What did you do in the city? How did my grandson manage to catch someone like you?”

Mydei answered honestly and politely. He told her about his burnout, his decision to move to the coast for a slower life, and how he’d met Phainon after nearly being run over by his scooter. The old woman listened carefully, nodding and occasionally chuckling at the story.

After a few more questions about his family and his tutoring job, she suddenly turned to Phainon.

“Sweetheart, go peel some apples and oranges for us in the kitchen. Use the good knife.”

Phainon opened his mouth to protest, but one look from his grandmother had him sighing and standing up. He gave Mydei a quick, sympathetic glance before disappearing into the tiny kitchen.

The moment he was gone, she leaned forward. “Mydei…” she began, her voice warm. “Let me speak honestly with you.”

She reached out and gently took his hand between her wrinkled ones.

“That boy has been carrying the world on his shoulders for too long. Ever since the bankruptcy, he works from sunrise until he can barely stand. He doesn’t complain, never asks for help. He’s forgotten how to let people in.” She gave a small, sad smile. “I was so worried about him. A young man shouldn’t live like that so alone.”

Her gaze drifted toward the kitchen for a moment before returning to Mydei.

“I feel guilty, you know. I raised him by myself after his parents abandoned us. We were poor, but we had love. Still… I couldn’t give him the childhood every child deserves. He barely had enough time to just be young and carefree. I did my best, but…” Her voice trembled slightly. “A grandmother wants more for her grandson.”

She squeezed Mydei’s hand.

“So thank you from the bottom of this old heart. Whether you two are friends, or something more… I can already see how different he is since you came into his life. He smiles more. His shoulders aren’t so heavy.”

She leaned in a little closer, voice dropping to a whisper.

“I only have one wish left in this life: that my Phainon finds someone who will love him the way he deserves. Someone who will stay when things get hard. Someone who sees the good, kind boy behind all that hard work.”

She gave him a watery but knowing smile.

“And I have a feeling… I might be looking at that person right now.”

Mydei felt his throat tighten. Before he could find the right words to respond, Phainon’s voice called from the kitchen.

“Grandma, are you interrogating him? I can hear you being emotional from here!”

The old woman laughed and wiped her eyes quickly. “Mind your own business and bring the fruit!”

Phainon returned a moment later carrying a plate of neatly peeled and sliced apples and oranges. He glanced between the two of them suspiciously.

“Everything okay?” he asked, sitting down beside Mydei and instinctively placing a hand on his knee.

Mydei smiled softly and covered Phainon’s hand with his own.

“Everything’s perfect,” he said, meaning it.

She watched them with a satisfied little smile that said she already approved.

“Eat,” she ordered gently. “And Mydei, you come visit me again soon. Without this one, if you want. I have more stories.”

Phainon groaned while Mydei laughed, warmth settling deep in his chest. He was really starting to feel like he belonged here.

---

After another round of tea and stories, the old woman eventually patted Mydei’s knee with a tired but content smile.

“I’m going to rest my eyes for a bit,” she said. “You boys clean up. And don’t break my good plates.”

She shuffled off to her bedroom, leaving the two of them alone in the small kitchen.

Mydei and Phainon stood side by side at the sink. For a while, they worked in comfortable silence, shoulders brushing every so often. Phainon eventually spoke, slightly amused.

“So… what did she tell you while I was peeling fruit?”

Mydei glanced at him, a small smile playing on his lips. “A lot of things. She told me stories about you as a kid. She also said she worries about you being alone.”

Phainon let out a soft sigh, scrubbing a plate a little harder than necessary.

“I figured.” He paused, then continued more quietly, “She’s always been scared I’ll end up lonely because of how hard I work. She thinks if I have someone by my side, she can finally stop worrying so much. I know she feels guilty about raising me alone… like she didn’t give me enough.”

He rinsed the plate and handed it to Mydei.

“I didn’t bring you here just so she could see that I’m not alone, though,” Phainon said, turning to look at him properly. “That’s not why.”

Mydei set the plate down and gave him his full attention. “Then why did you bring me?”

Phainon leaned his hip against the counter.

“Because you’re important to me. Really important.” His voice softened. “I told you about my debts, my jobs, my grandmother… all the heavy parts of my life. I wanted you to meet her for the same reason. I want you to know every piece of me. The good, the messy, the complicated.”

He reached out and gently took Mydei’s soapy hand.

“You’re not just someone I’m dating or seeing. I want you engraved in my life, Mydei. I want you to know my grandma, and I want her to know you. Because I’m hoping… this thing between us is going to last.”

The honesty in his voice made Mydei’s chest tighten with warmth. He stepped closer, wrapping his arms around Phainon’s waist, his hands soaking into his shirt.

“I want that too,” Mydei whispered against his neck. “I want to be part of your life. All of it.”

Phainon exhaled in relief and hugged him back tightly, burying his face in Mydei’s shoulder for a long moment. When he pulled back, his eyes were softer.

“Good,” he murmured, leaning in to press a tender kiss to Mydei’s lips. “I’m not planning on letting you go anytime soon. Or not ever.”

“One hundred percent agree. Donʼt ever let go.”

---

A few days later, Mydei arrived at the Kostas house for Caelus’s usual tutoring session, carrying his notebook and a couple of new reading materials. As he climbed the stairs to the apartment, he noticed a second pair of school shoes neatly placed on the porch beside Caelus’s sneakers.

Must have a friend over, he thought with a small smile. Good. Maybe it’ll make today’s session less painful.

He knocked twice, then let himself in as he usually did after Mr. Kostas had told him it was fine.

The moment he stepped inside, the atmosphere felt off. The living room was empty. He could hear muffled, hurried whispering coming from the direction of Caelus’s bedroom. Mydei approached slowly and knocked on the door.

“Caelus? It’s me.”

There was a moment of silence, then some frantic rustling.

When Mydei gently pushed the door open, he found two boys sitting stiffly on the edge of the bed, looking like they’d been caught committing a crime. Caelus’s face was flushed red, his hair more messy than usual. Beside him sat another boy, whose hair a little bit tousled, and he was calm but slightly nervous. He was also wearing the same school uniform.

They were both fully dressed, but the rumpled sheets, the way they refused to look at each other, and the obvious tension in the air told Mydei everything he needed to know.

Caelus looked like he wanted the floor to swallow him whole.

The other boy recovered first. He stood up politely, though his ears were also pink, and gave a small bow of his head.

“Hello, sir. You must be Mr. Mydei, Caelus’s English tutor,” he said with surprising composure. “I’m Dan Heng. I’m… Caelus’s boyfriend.”

Caelus made a strangled, embarrassed noise and buried his face in his hands. “Dan Heng—!”

Mydei blinked, processing the situation. He cleared his throat, trying to keep his expression neutral and professional despite the mild surprise.

“I see,” he said carefully. “Nice to meet you, Dan Heng.” He paused, then added with a hint of dry amusement, “Maybe next time you two could… study in the living room?”

Caelus groaned loudly. “This is so embarrassing. Please don’t tell my dad.”

Mydei sighed and leaned against the doorframe, crossing his arms.

“I’m not going to tell your father about your personal life,” he reassured them. “But I do expect you to be more responsible. You’re fourteen. And I’m here for your lesson, not to walk in on… whatever this was.”

Dan Heng nodded seriously, looking genuinely apologetic. “We understand. It won’t happen again during your tutoring hours.”

Caelus peeked through his fingers, still mortified. “Are you… mad?”

Mydei softened a little.

“I’m not mad. Just surprised. And a little concerned.” He gestured toward the living room. “Come on. Bring your books. Dan Heng can stay if he wants, as long as you both actually focus on English today.”

The two boys shuffled out of the bedroom, Caelus still blushing furiously and Dan Heng staying impressively calm. Apparently, even the edgy teenager he was tutoring had more romantic drama going on than he did.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Domestic Routine
chapters.html:
The lesson eventually resumed. After some initial awkwardness, the atmosphere slowly returned to normal. Dan Heng turned out to be incredibly well-mannered and smart. He even helped explain a few grammar points to Caelus in a calm, patient way that actually made the boy listen. By the end of the hour, they had covered more material than usual.

Dan Heng stood up first, politely saying goodbye to Mydei before giving Caelus a quick, shy glance.

“I’ll text you later,” he said softly, then slipped out of the apartment.

Once they were alone, Caelus became visibly restless. Mydei gathered his things and was about to head out when Caelus suddenly spoke.

“Um… Mr. Mydei?” he mumbled, not meeting his eyes. “Can we… go get some snacks? There’s a convenience store nearby.”

Mr. Mydei? Mydei paused, studying the boy’s tense shoulders. He immediately understood this wasn’t really about snacks.

“Sure,” he said gently. “Let’s go.”

They walked to the small store in silence. Caelus bought a bag of chips and two cans of soda. Mydei got himself a cold coffee. They ended up sitting on a bench under a shady tree near the harbor, the afternoon sun filtering through the leaves.

They ate without speaking for a few minutes. Finally, Caelus broke the silence.

“You… you really won’t tell my dad, right? About Dan Heng and me.”

Mydei looked at him for a moment, then set his coffee down.

“I promised I wouldn’t. And I keep my promises, Caelus.”

Caelus nodded, but he still looked anxious, picking at the edge of the chip bag.

Mydei realized a simple “yes” wasn’t going to be enough. He exhaled softly and spoke again, gentler this time.

“Actually… I understand more than you might think.”

Caelus glanced at him curiously.

Mydei continued, “I like men too. In fact, I’m currently seeing someone. A guy.”

Caelus’s eyes widened in surprise. “Wait… seriously?”

“Yeah,” Mydei said with a small smile. “His name is Phainon. He’s the one who almost ran me over with his scooter the day I moved here. We’ve been seeing each other for a while now.”

He paused, letting the words settle.

“So when you worry about your dad finding out, or what people might say… I’ve been there. I know how scary it can feel, especially at your age. But I also know that having someone who genuinely cares about you makes a lot of the fear worth it.”

Caelus stayed quiet for a moment, processing everything. His shoulders slowly relaxed.

“…Does it get easier?” he asked quietly.

Mydei nodded. “It does. Especially when you have people who support you. And even if your dad reacts badly at first, I think he loves you enough to eventually understand.”

Caelus let out a long breath, the tension finally draining from his face. For the first time that day, he gave Mydei a smile.

“Thanks… for not being weird about it. And for telling me.”

Mydei smiled back and lightly ruffled the boy’s messy hair.

“Anytime. Now finish your chips before they get stale.”

They sat together on the bench a while longer, the silence between them much more comfortable now.

---

One afternoon, Caelus and Dan Heng were walking home together after school when Caelus tugged on Dan Heng’s sleeve.

“Let’s get some snacks first. I’m starving.”

Dan Heng nodded quietly, always happy to spend a little more time with him. They stepped into the small convenience store near the harbor. The bell above the door chimed as they entered.

While they were browsing the snack aisle, Caelus suddenly froze near the counter.

Behind the register, wearing the store’s green apron over a black t-shirt, was Phainon. His newly dyed gray hair was slightly messy, and he looked a little tired but still unfairly handsome as he scanned items for another customer.

Phainon glanced up out of habit, and their eyes met. For a brief second, recognition flashed across both their faces. Phainon had seen Caelus a couple of times when he dropped Mydei off near the Kostas house. Caelus obviously knew exactly who Phainon was.

But neither of them acknowledged anything beyond politeness.

Phainon gave a small nod. “Hey.”

Caelus nodded back, equally casual. “Hey.”

That was it.

Caelus and Dan Heng quickly paid for their chips and drinks. As they left the store, Phainon gave another polite nod and said, “Have a good evening,” in his usual friendly tone.

“You too,” Caelus replied before grabbing the bag and heading toward the door where Dan Heng was waiting.

Once they were outside and a good distance away from the store, Caelus casually popped a chip into his mouth and said, “That guy’s my tutor’s boyfriend.”

Dan Heng, who had been quietly sipping his drink, nearly choked.

“Wait… seriously?” He blinked, clearly surprised. “The tall one with the gray hair? Phainon?”

“Yeah. Mydei’s dating him.” Caelus opened the bag of chips and offered some to Dan Heng. “I’ve seen him a few times when he comes to pick up Mydei.”

Dan Heng’s expression visibly relaxed. A small, relieved smile tugged at his lips.

“Oh. That’s good.” He accepted the chips, ears slightly pink. “For a second I thought you also found him cute and I was going to have competition with a grown adult.”

Caelus laughed loudly, nearly choking on his soda.

“Are you jealous?”

“No,” Dan Heng said too quickly, then quieter, “…Maybe a little.”

Caelus grinned and leaned closer, bumping their hands together.

“Relax. He’s hot, sure… but Mydei’s the one dating him. I only have eyes for one person right now.”

Dan Heng’s expression softened instantly. A small, shy smile appeared on his lips as he glanced sideways at Caelus.

“…Good.”

They continued walking, the plastic bag of snacks rustling between them.

Caelus eventually spoke again. “Mydei’s actually pretty cool about us.”

Dan Heng nodded slowly, reaching over to lightly hook his pinky with Caelus’s.

“Guess we’re lucky to have a tutor like him.”

Caelus didn’t pull his hand away.

“Yeah,” he muttered, cheeks slightly pink. “We are.”

---

A few evenings later, Mydei and Phainon met near the harbor after Phainon finished his shift. The sun had just set, leaving the sky in soft purples and oranges as they walked side by side.

Instead of heading toward Phainon’s apartment as they often did, Mydei gently caught his hand.

“Hey,” he said, “why don’t you come over to my place tonight? I’ll cook for you for a change. There’s also something I want to talk to you about.”

Phainon raised an eyebrow, a playful smile tugging at his lips. “You’re cooking? And you want to talk? Should I be worried?”

Mydei laughed and squeezed his hand. “It’s nothing bad. Just an idea I’ve been thinking about.”

“Alright, I’m in.”

When they arrived at the little blue house, the evening air was cool and fragrant with wild thyme. Mydei opened the windows to let the sea breeze in while Phainon rolled up his sleeves, immediately making something in the kitchen.

Tonight’s dinner was simple: grilled fish with lemon and herbs, roasted vegetables, and a fresh salad. While the fish was sizzling in the pan, Mydei finally brought up what was on his mind.

“So… I’ve been thinking about using the front yard,” he said, nodding toward the open window. “It’s mostly just grass and some weeds right now. I want to turn it into a vegetable patch. Tomatoes, zucchini, peppers, maybe some herbs. What do you think?”

Phainon leaned over to look outside, then turned back with a bright, genuine smile.

“I think that’s a great idea. The soil here is pretty good, and you get decent sun most of the day.” He bumped Mydei’s shoulder. “Need help planning it? I used to help grandma with her garden all the time. I know which spots get the best drainage.”

Mydei’s face lit up. “I was hoping you’d say that. I don’t know the first thing about gardening. I was a city boy, remember?”

Phainon chuckled and slid an arm around Mydei’s waist from behind, resting his chin on his shoulder as they watched the fish cook.

“I’ll help you. We can start on the weekend if you want. I’ll bring some tools and good compost from the community garden.” He pressed a soft kiss to the side of Mydei’s neck. “It’ll be nice having fresh vegetables from your own yard. We can cook with them together.”

Mydei leaned back into his embrace, warmth spreading through his chest.

“I like the sound of that. ‘Our’ vegetables,” he murmured.

Phainon’s arms tightened around him. “Yeah,” he said softly. “Ours.”

They stayed in the same position, savoring the closeness, before Phainon reluctantly let go so they could finish preparing dinner.

Later, they ate outside on the small terrace. The sound of waves in the distance and strings of fairy lights glowed above them. Between bites and easy conversation, Phainon kept reaching over to touch Mydei’s hand or brush his knee like a constant reminder that he was happy to be here.

Mydei watched him across the table, heart feeling wonderfully full.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Life of Me
chapters.html:
Phainon returned that evening just after sunset, bone-tired from a long day of deliveries and an extra shift at the restaurant. But the moment he stepped through the gate of the little blue house, all the exhaustion seemed to melt off his shoulders. A giddy, boyish smile stayed plastered on his face the entire ride back.

He was still smiling when he pushed open the front door. The sight that greeted him made his chest tighten with affection.

Mydei had fallen asleep at the dining table. He was still wearing the light blue apron Phainon had bought him as a joke weeks ago, one cheek resting on his folded arms. A few dishes were already set on the table, and the smell of baked herbs and lemon chicken lingered in the air. The poor man had clearly tried to wait up for him.

Phainon’s heart did a ridiculous little flip.

He set down the small box of pastries he’d brought from the bakery and walked over softly. Leaning down, he pressed a gentle kiss to the top of Mydei’s head, breathing in the scent of his shampoo mixed with cooking smells.

Mydei stirred almost immediately, letting out a small, sleepy hum.

“…Phainon?” he mumbled, voice rough with sleep. He blinked slowly, lifting his head. A faint crease from his sleeve was pressed into his cheek.

“Yeah, it’s me,” Phainon whispered, brushing stray hair from Mydei’s forehead. “You fell asleep waiting for me. Looks like someone overdid it today.”

Mydei sat up straighter, rubbing his eyes. “I wanted to have everything ready when you got back… Guess I dozed off.”

Phainon’s smile softened further. He leaned down again and kissed Mydei properly this time.

“You didn’t have to. But thank you.” He glanced at the table. “It smells amazing.”

They reheated the chicken and vegetables together. Mydei moved a little stiffly, still clearly feeling the aftereffects of last night, which only made Phainon hover around him more protectively.

Once everything was warm, they sat down to eat. Even though Phainon had been running around all day, he looked lighter, almost glowing with happiness.

“You’ve been smiling nonstop since you walked in,” Mydei observed, amused. “Good day?”

Phainon reached across the table and took Mydei’s hand, thumb brushing over his knuckles.

“Not particularly,” he admitted. “But I kept thinking about waking up next to you this morning… and coming home to this.” He gestured at the table, then at Mydei wearing the apron. “It made the whole day feel easy.”

Mydei’s cheeks warmed. He squeezed Phainon’s hand back.

“Sounds like you wanna be here every night.”

“…Would that be so bad?” Phainon asked softly.

Mydei looked at him for a moment across the candlelit table.

“No,” he answered quietly. “It wouldn’t.”

They finished dinner slowly, exchanging soft words and lingering touches. Afterward, Phainon refused to let Mydei clean up, gently pushing him toward the couch instead.

“Rest,” he said, kissing Mydei’s temple. “I’ve got this. You already did more than enough today.”

As Phainon moved around the kitchen, humming quietly to himself, Mydei watched him with a content, sleepy smile.

This little blue house had never felt more like home.

On Phainon’s rare day off a few days later, the two of them woke up together in Mydei’s bed. After a slow morning and a leisurely breakfast, Phainon stretched his arms above his head and grinned.

“How about we turn that front yard into something useful today?”

They rode Phainon’s scooter to the local hardware store on the edge of town. It was an old, dusty place that sold everything from paint to farming tools. The moment they stepped inside, Phainon’s excitement became contagious.

They walked through the aisles side by side, picking out materials for the raised garden beds. Phainon carefully chose sturdy wooden planks, while Mydei read the backs of seed packets with adorable concentration.

“Should we do tomatoes first?” Mydei asked, holding up two different varieties.

Phainon leaned over his shoulder, resting his chin there. “Get both. And zucchini. You liked the ones we cooked last week, right?”

They ended up buying far more than originally planned. They got wooden beams, soil, compost, several packets of seeds (tomatoes, zucchini, peppers, basil, and cucumbers), gloves, a watering can, and even a cute kneeling pad that Phainon insisted Mydei would need.

At the checkout, the elderly owner smiled at them knowingly as he rang up their items.

“You two building a garden together? How sweet.”

Phainon didn’t miss a beat. He wrapped an arm around Mydei’s waist and replied with a proud grin, “Yes sir. First garden for my husband here.”

Mydei elbowed him lightly, but he didn’t pull away.

When they finally loaded everything onto the scooter (and a borrowed cart), Phainon looked at the pile of supplies, then at Mydei, and let out a soft laugh.

“God… this really feels like we’re married,” he said. “Going to the hardware store together, arguing over which tomato seeds are better, buying matching gloves… I keep waiting for someone to ask me how long we’ve been together.”

Mydei turned to him. A small, fond smile played on his lips.

“Would that be so bad?” he asked, echoing Phainon’s words from a few nights ago.

Phainon’s expression softened. He stepped closer and cupped Mydei’s face with both hands, thumbs gently brushing his cheeks.

“No,” he said quietly. “It wouldn’t be bad at all. I kinda like it.”

He leaned in and kissed Mydei right there in the hardware store parking lot, not caring who might see.

“Let’s go home and start building our garden… husband,” he teased softly.

Phainon’s eyes sparkled with happiness.

“Yes, husband.”

They rode back to the little blue house with supplies tied precariously on the scooter, both of them smiling like idiots the entire way.

They got straight to work on the front yard right away.

The patch was more overgrown than Mydei remembered. There were tall grass, stubborn weeds, and a few wild bushes that had claimed the space. They started early while the sun was still gentle, pulling weeds and clearing the ground.

It didn’t take long for Mydei to start sweating. After about forty minutes, he straightened up and tugged his damp t-shirt off, tossing it onto the nearby bench.

Phainon, who had been focused on digging out a particularly stubborn root, completely lost his rhythm. His eyes kept drifting over to Mydei’s bare torso. He watched the sweat glistened on his skin, the subtle flex of muscle as he worked, and the faint red marks Phainon had left on his neck and collarbone just nights ago.

Mydei noticed after the third long glance.

“Phainon,” he said, half-amused, half-exasperated. “Focus on the garden, not me.”

Phainon leaned on his shovel, wiping sweat from his own brow with the back of his gloved hand. A mischievous grin spread across his face.

“Can’t help it,” he replied shamelessly. “You’re way more interesting than weeds.”

Mydei shook his head, trying to hide his smile. He bent down to pull another clump of grass when Phainon suddenly spoke again.

“Hey, Mydei.”

“Hm?”

“What’s the similarity between you and this garden?”

Mydei paused, suspicious. He straightened up and raised an eyebrow. “I don’t know. What?”

Phainon’s grin turned wicked. He stepped closer, voice dropping into a husky murmur.

“Because I’m gonna plow both of you thoroughly… and then plant my seeds real deep.”

Mydei stared at him for a second, stunned. Then he let out a loud, incredulous laugh, cheeks flushing despite himself.

“Oh my God,” he groaned, covering his face with one dirty glove. “That was terrible. Absolutely horrible.”

Phainon laughed too, clearly proud of himself. He closed the distance between them and wrapped his arms around Mydei’s bare waist, pulling their sweaty bodies together.

“You’re laughing though,” he teased, pressing a kiss to Mydei’s shoulder. “Means it was at least a little funny.”

“You’re ridiculous,” Mydei muttered, but he tilted his head to give Phainon better access anyway. “We’re never going to finish this garden if you keep distracting me like this.”

Phainon hummed, lips brushing against Mydei’s ear.

“Who said I wanted to finish it today?” His hands slid lower, squeezing Mydei’s ass. “We could always continue tomorrow.”

Mydei shivered despite the warm sun on his back. He turned in Phainon’s arms and gave him a slow, heated kiss on his lips.

“You’re going to be the death of me.”

Phainon smiled against his mouth.

“And youʼre going to be the life of me.”
